AX-RadioLAB                                                                                      www.onsemi.com

for AX5043 User Manual                                                              APPLICATION NOTE

Introduction:                                                     The first step in working with AX-RadioLAB is to create
  The AX-RadioLAB is hands on configuration and                 a new AX-RadioLAB project. Firmware projects
                                                                implementing the TX and RX mode selected in the
firmware source code generation tool for the AX5043             AX-RadioLAB GUI are created inside your project
transceiver IC.                                                 directory.

  It creates C-code firmware projects based on the                The AX-RadioLAB GUI makes it easy to configure
AXRadio2 API (described in DOCU/AXRadioV2API.pdf),              physical parameters of the wireless link as well as the
which demonstrate the use of the AX5043 transceiver             framing format and various possible functions of the
together with the AX8052F100 micro controller for packet        AX5043 general purpose pins.
transmission and reception in several modes. Packets can be
transmitted periodically or upon pressing a button. On the        Optionally you can view and modify the generated
receiver side the available options are:                        firmware source code using the AXCode::Blocks IDE. The
                                                                firmware also makes a nice starting point for your own
· RX continuous (RX is always on)                               development. You can always use AX-RadioLAB
· Wake on Radio                                                 to modify wireless parameters of your project, even after
· RX Synchronized with TX (The RX is on for the time            modifying the firmware.

   in which packets are expected only).

  Optionally received packets can be answered with
an acknowledge packet in all modes.

  AX-RadioLAB allows direct downloading of the created
firmware to AXSEM DVK-2 main boards and AXSEM
F143-MINI-DVM, where it can be run and tested
immediately. A dedicated firmware project implements
basic tests like putting the transmitter into CW mode or
measuring bit error rates.

Software Requirements:                                          installed, the installer automatically uninstalls previous
   For AX-RadioLAB to work correctly you need to install        versions of AX-RadioLAB. Run setup.exe again to install.
                                                                At the end of the each process you will be asked to reboot
the AX8052-IDE first. Install all sub-components of the         your computer. This is not necessary.
AX8052-IDE (AXSDB, SDCC, driver, AXCode::Blocks).

  Execute the setup.exe to start the installation
of AX-RadioLAB. If AX-RadioLAB was already

and SYNC WORD bytes before writing them to the firmware code if "unencoded" and INV encoding are selected.

   the frequency tracker (AFC) can walk in either           The TX measures the channel RSSI before sending

Framing Mode:                                                  · Occasionally it may be necessary to conclude the
  Options are HDLC, Raw Pattern Match and PN9
                                                                  preamble with a few special bits. This can be achieved
Compatibility. in Raw Pattern Match mode an arbitrary             using the fields below "Append additional encoded
SYNC WORD of up to 32 bit marks the beginning                     bits".
of a frame. For legacy systems the PN9 Compatibility mode
implements PN9 data whitening in software, based on the        SYNC WORD
AX5043's Raw Pattern Match mode.
                                                               · In Raw Preamble Mode you can choose an arbitrary
Preamble:
                                                                  sync word of up to 32 bit as a start of frame delimiter.
· Recommended default settings are chosen according               However it is recommended to use a sync word with

· "RX PN9", "TX PN9", "RX PN15", "TX PN15", "RX

   PN17", "TX PN17" are similar to "RX 1010" and "TX

3 The "RX1010", "RX PN9", "RX PN15" and "RX PN17" modes periodically settle the receiver with aggressive settings of the receiver tracking
loops (RX parameters set 0) and then switch to the less aggressive settings (RX parameter set 3), where for instance the AGC loop is frozen
completely. This is similar the situation of packet reception, where RX parameter set 3 is used after detection of a SYNC WORD. When
measuring the bit error rate with external instrumentation this approach cannot be used. Receiving with RX parameter set 0 may lead
to an increased bit error rate, while permanently receiving with RX parameter set 3 would not allow the AGC to settle. The "Output RX via DATA
pin" therefore uses a variant of RX parameter set 3 where the AGC is running, typically with 1/4 of the bandwidth of the RX parameter set
0 settings.

contains the rx_margin used in normal operation

NOTE:  A processing delay occurs in the RX, i.e. the
       detection of the SFD is not signalled by the RX
       the very moment it is on air. On the other RX
       should be enabled rx_margin before the packet
       is on air. Therefore dt_SFD is not simply the
       length of preamble plus SFD but also contains
       the processing delay of roughly 19 bit.
